pairs.subject: motion
pairs.evidence: app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:94 The float and pulse ambient presets loop forever on empty-state heroes with no visible stop control and no in-view or foreground veto, so self-starting motion runs past the five-second threshold with nothing that stops it except the OS reduce-motion query; on top of that, the presets inline raw easing and seconds, and the worst-case entrance overruns the library's own cap.

techniques.evidence: app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:94 The float (and pulse, line 108) loop starts by itself, runs indefinitely and has no visible, operable stop. The prop API offers no stop control at all.

app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:140 The only IntersectionObserver controls entrance replay, and the comment at line 26 says ambient loops keep their own clock. The loop's only veto is the CSS media query: there is no merged in-view, foreground or user-stop signal.

app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:69 Presets have one home, an intent docstring each, a per-preset fallback and a reachability test, but they inline raw seconds and a raw curve. The same curve is retyped in globals.css, CandidateModal, StudioZone, atlas.css and the about stage. No duration-class or easing-role token exists.

app/_components/glyph/MotionizedGlyph.tsx:106 stagger is 0.08 + delay*1.1, plus 0.5s. With devCasesGlyph's max delay of 0.744 the entrance takes about 1.40s, past the '<= ~1.2s' guardrail at motionPresets.ts:15. The delay test allows up to 1.68s, so the cap is prose only.

app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:111 Latent: no preset reaches this today. In glyphMotionCss.ts, around lines 46-52, the renderer keeps a loop running under reduced motion when the loop declares 'opacity-only', on the reasoning that opacity carries no vestibular motion. The technique says infinite loops reduce to stillness whatever property they animate. Current loops declare 'none' and are stilled. Per-preset fallbacks and the opacity:0 resting-state fix are done correctly.

app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:96 The glyph is decorative (aria-hidden by default). When a preset is stilled, glyphMotionCss.ts restores opacity:1, so the resting opacity:0 cannot delete the drawing under reduced motion.
app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:9 Scoped CSS keyframes were chosen on purpose for a non-interruptible declarative timeline over many paths. No library-level global switch can turn it off.
app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:67 Every preset animates only transform and opacity, and no frame value passes through React state.
app/_components/glyph/motionPresets.ts:131 Entrance and ambient are separate tracks with their own timing, assembled in sequence (the loop starts after the entrance settles). A test pins this.

pairs.registryProposal: reduced-motion-mechanics could add an explicit example: a renderer branch that keeps an opacity-only loop running under reduced motion is the named failure, even when no current preset uses it.

pairs.subject: motion
pairs.evidence: app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:27 Each motion.div decides its own reduced-motion variant and inlines its own durations and easing, so reduction is a parallel implementation at each call site instead of a preset-level fallback, and nothing ties these gestures to a shared vocabulary.

techniques.evidence: app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:27 There are five separate `reduced ?` branches at call sites, which the technique names as the failure ('call sites never branch'). The reveal-quiet placeholder does keep its anti-flash delay under reduced motion, which is correct.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:53 Durations and easing are inline literals, and no named preset is referenced.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:51 Only opacity and y (transform) are animated. The height delta goes through framer's transform-based layout tween.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:65 Every gesture is 250ms or less and enters decelerate, with 6px travel.

app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:61 The wrapper stays mounted and tweens its height, and the placeholder reserves the result's height. The inner pending-to-result swap is a short sequential fade (mode=wait), not two elements overlapping. A shared layoutId would be the stronger rung.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:67 initial={false} means a card that mounts with a cached answer shows it settled. Only a real state change animates.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:50 Under reduced motion the verdict still renders, with a brief fade and no travel. Content is never withheld.

app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:9 Framer is used for mount and unmount presence. A repo search found no MotionConfig or LazyMotion, so no global framer switch can silently disable these gestures.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:112 The pulsing loop was removed. The panel now has only triggered one-shot transitions, nothing that runs longer than five seconds.
app/features/shared/MatchReasoningPanel.tsx:115 The placeholder is a static box with a one-shot hold. There is no loop to pause.
